arxiv-1911-13032.title: Safe Walking In VR using Augmented Virtuality
arxiv-1911-13032.creator: Maurício Sousa, Daniel Mendes, and Joaquim Jorge
arxiv-1911-13032.description: Abstract New technologies allow ordinary people to access Virtual Reality at affordable prices in their homes. One of the most important tasks when interacting with immersive Virtual Reality is to navigate the virtual environments (VEs). Arguably, the best methods to accomplish this use direct control interfaces. Among those, natural walking (NW) makes for an enjoyable user experience.

arxiv-2206-12886.title: Detection of 16 small glitches in 9 pulsars
arxiv-2206-12886.creator: Zu-Rong Zhou, Jing-Bo Wang, Na Wang, Jian-Ping Yuan, Fei-Fei Kou, Shi-Jun Dang
arxiv-2206-12886.description: Abstract Timing observations from the Nanshan 26-m radio telescope for nine pulsars between 2000 and 2014 have been used to search for glitches. The data span for nine pulsars ranges from 11.6 to 14.2 years. From the total of 114 yr of pulsar rotational history, 16 new glitches were identified in 9 pulsars.

arxiv-2307-04805.title: The Dragon-II simulations - I. Evolution of single and binary compact objects in star clusters with up to 1 million stars 2020 The Dragon-II simulations - I. Evolution of single and binary compact objects in star clusters with up to 1 million stars – References
arxiv-2307-04805.creator: Manuel Arca Sedda, Albrecht W. H. Kamlah, Rainer Spurzem, Mirek Giersz, Peter Berczik, Sara Rastello, Giuliano Iorio, Michela Mapelli, Massimiliano Gatto, Eva K. Grebel
arxiv-2307-04805.description: Abstract We present the first results of the Dragon-II simulations, a suite of 19 N N -body simulations of star clusters with up to 10 6 10^{6} stars, with up to 33 % 33\% of them initially paired in binaries. In this work, we describe the main evolution of the clusters and their compact objects (COs).

arxiv-2311-16865.title: A Benchmark for Evaluating Machine Translation Metrics on Dialects Without Standard Orthography
arxiv-2311-16865.creator: Noëmi Aepli Chantal Amrhein Florian Schottmann Rico Sennrich
arxiv-2311-16865.description: Abstract For sensible progress in natural language processing, it is important that we are aware of the limitations of the evaluation metrics we use. In this work, we evaluate how robust metrics are to non-standardized dialects, i.e. spelling differences in language varieties that do not have a standard orthography.

arxiv-2511-01654.title: Panther: A Cost-Effective Privacy-Preserving Framework for GNN Training and Inference Services in Cloud Environments
arxiv-2511-01654.creator: Congcong Chen, Xinyu Liu, Kaifeng Huang, Lifei Wei, Yang Shi
arxiv-2511-01654.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have marked significant impact in traffic state prediction, social recommendation, knowledge-aware question answering and so on. As more and more users move towards cloud computing, it has become a critical issue to unleash the power of GNNs while protecting the privacy in cloud environments.

arxiv-2602-16147.title: ASPEN: Spectral-Temporal Fusion for Cross-Subject Brain Decoding Thanks: Code available at https://github.com/meganmlee/ASPEN
arxiv-2602-16147.creator: Megan Lee, Seung Ha Hwang, Inhyeok Choi, Shreyas Darade, Mengchun Zhang, Kateryna Shapovalenko
arxiv-2602-16147.description: Abstract Cross-subject generalization in EEG-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) remains challenging due to individual variability in neural signals. We investigate whether spectral representations offer more stable features for cross-subject transfer than temporal waveforms. Through correlation analyses across three EEG paradigms (SSVEP, P300, and Motor Imagery), we find that spectral features exhibit consistently higher cross-subject similarity than temporal signals.

pmc-10536920.title: An Assessment of Environmental RF Noise Due to IoT Deployment
pmc-10536920.creator: Dominique G K Ingala, Nelendran Pillay, Aritha Pillay, Antonio Puliafito
pmc-10536920.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The advent of the Internet of Things (IoT) has contributed to an increase in the production volume of RF-featured equipment. According to statistics from the literature, the IoT industry will soon deploy billions of products. While the concept behind these applications seems exciting, this paper sought to assess the effects the radio emissions produced by IoT products would have on the ambient radio noise levels within the unlicensed frequency bands of 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 2.4 GHz.

pmc-11325822.description: BackgroundGiven the geographical sparsity of Rare Diseases (RDs), assembling a cohort is often a challenging task. Common data models (CDM) can harmonize disparate sources of data that can be the basis of decision support systems and artificial intelligence-based studies, leading to new insights in the field.

pmc-11508667.title: The Influence of Age and Exercise Training Status on Left Ventricular Systolic Twist Mechanics in Healthy Males—An Exploratory Study
pmc-11508667.creator: Alexander J Beaumont, Amy K Campbell, Viswanath B Unnithan, David Oxborough, Fergal Grace, Allan Knox, Nicholas F Sculthorpe, Giuseppe Caminiti
pmc-11508667.description: Age-related differences in twist may be mitigated with exercise training, although this remains inconclusive. Moreover, temporal left ventricular (LV) systolic twist mechanics, including early-systolic (twistearly), and beyond peak twist (twistpeak) alone, have not been considered. Therefore, further insights are required to ascertain the influence of age and training status on twist mechanics across systole.

pmc-12598319.title: Feasibility study of the Cambridge knee injury tool (CamKIT): 18-month analysis of acute knee injuries at an urgent treatment centre☆
pmc-12598319.creator: Thomas Molloy, Benjamin Gompels, Simone Castagno, Andrew McCaskie, Stephen McDonnell
pmc-12598319.description: BackgroundSoft tissue knee injuries are associated with many short- and long-term consequences. Currently, obstacles in the diagnostic pathway lead to inefficiencies in the management process, resulting in suboptimal patient outcomes. Early stratification of knee injury severity is essential for guiding timely investigations and management decisions.

pmc-13365561.title: BAI adhesion-GPCRs perform distinct functions in neural development differentially controlled by RTN4R and C1ql ligands
pmc-13365561.creator: Jie Wang, Jinzhao Wang, Yi Miao, Yang Li, Shaoyuan Zhu, Yu Zhang, Ahmed Yousif, Min Huang, Marius Wernig, Thomas C. Südhof
pmc-13365561.description: BAI1, BAI2, and BAI3 (for ‘Brain-specific Angiogenesis Inhibitor-1, -2, and -3’) are adhesion-GPCRs implicated in neuronal development. The precise roles of individual BAIs remain unclear. BAIs interact with two sets of ligands, secreted C1ql proteins and membrane-bound RTN4R proteins (a.k.a. NoGo receptors), but which of these ligands regulate specific functions of BAIs is incompletely understood.

pmc-13630960.title: Monomeric CRP is prevalent in the blood of patients with rheumatoid arthritis and correlates with clinically relevant markers
pmc-13630960.creator: Alexia Correia Ferreira, Lucia Martin-Gutierrez, Christophe Lalaurie, Karen Feehan, Priyanka Lakhani, Imogen Buckle, George A. Robinson, Elizabeth C. Jury, Jessica J. Manson, Thomas C. R. McDonnell
pmc-13630960.description: IntroductionElevated C-reactive protein (CRP) is a hallmark of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares. CRP exists as pentameric (pCRP) and monomeric (mCRP) isoforms with distinct functions, with pCRP generally pro-inflammatory and mCRP more immunomodulatory. Standard clinical assays do not distinguish between these forms, and it remains unclear whether elevated CRP in RA reflects structural variation.
